scenes.title: Arrival at Poseidon's Sacrifice
scenes.card: They arrive during a great sacrifice to the sea god; shy Telemachus is urged forward; Nestor's son welcomes them to the feast.

subs.text: Book three.
King Nestor Remembers.
Scene one.
Arrival at Poseidon's Sacrifice.
At sunrise the ship reaches Pylos, where nine great divisions sacrifice black bulls to Poseidon.
How do I even greet such a man?
I have no practice in careful speech.
Telemachus, no more shyness, not now;
you crossed the sea for your father's sake.
Go straight up to Nestor, breaker of horses, and ask him what counsel he keeps in his breast.
Some words you will find in yourself, and a god will set the rest on your tongue,
for the gods have not left you unattended from your birth.
Welcome.
Come inside, take food, and speak when you are ready.
Hear me, Poseidon, girdler of the earth.
Grant fame to Nestor and his sons, grace to all Pylos in return for this rich hecatomb,
and grant that Telemachus and I accomplish the errand we sailed here to do.

scenes.title: Telemachus Questions Nestor
scenes.card: Nestor asks who the strangers are; Telemachus names himself and begs for the plain truth about his father.

subs.text: Scene two.
Telemachus Questions Nestor.
Strangers, now that you have had your pleasure of the feast, it is fair to ask:
who are you?
From where do you sail the watery ways?
Is it on business, or do you rove at hazard like raiders,
who risk their own lives to bring evil upon other men?
Nestor, son of Neleus, great glory of the Achaeans, we come from Ithaca below Neion, and the errand is my own:
my father, hard-enduring Odysseus, who fought at your side and sacked the city of Troy.
I beg you, do not soften anything out of pity for me;
tell me exactly what your own eyes saw or what word has reached you.
Friend, you bring it all back, what we suffered on that plain, and the best of us fallen:
Ajax lies there, and Achilles, and Patroclus wise as the gods, and my own strong Antilochus.
And in every craft of war your father had no rival;
no man alive could match Odysseus for cunning.
Truly you are his son, your very speech is his.
Nestor begins the account of the quarrel that split the returning Greek fleet.

scenes.title: The Broken Return from Troy
scenes.card: Nestor remembers how the Greek fleet split after the war; Odysseus went another way, and Nestor never learned what became of him.

subs.text: Scene three.
The Broken Return from Troy.
The two sons of Atreus called the army to assembly at sunset, a reckless hour,
and stood and quarreled before us all.
Menelaus said sail, sail now over the sea's broad back;
Agamemnon would hold the host and slaughter hecatombs to appease Athena's wrath.
Fool, for she was not to be turned so, and we split in two, and the night was ugly with shouting.
Half the fleet sailed.
Odysseus turned back to support Agamemnon.
Nestor, Diomedes, and Menelaus escaped by a difficult route and reached home.
But of Odysseus I can tell you only what has drifted to my hearth, for I came home with no news of my own.
They say the Myrmidons came safe, and Philoctetes, and Idomeneus lost not a man the war had spared;
but of your father, living or dead, no traveler has brought me one certain word.

scenes.title: Orestes as the Measure
scenes.card: Nestor tells how Agamemnon was murdered at home and his son Orestes avenged him, and urges Telemachus to be just as brave.

subs.text: Scene four.
Orestes as the Measure.
You know how Aegisthus, while we bled at Troy, sat safe in horse-pasturing Argos and charmed Agamemnon's wife,
and how he cut the king down at his own hearth on the day of his homecoming.
But payment came for it:
in the eighth year Orestes returned from Athens and killed his father's murderer,
and all the Argives honored him for the deed.
And you, my friend, tall and fine as I see you are, be brave, so that men not yet born will speak well of you.
Do not wander long away from home while those proud men sit in your halls and eat everything you have.
If only the gods would give me strength like that.
But they will not, not for me, not for my father.
Telemachus, what word has escaped the barrier of your teeth?
Easily, when he wills it, a god brings a man safe home from the ends of the earth.
Better long roads and hard travel and a late return than to come home swiftly and die at your own hearth,
as Agamemnon died.

scenes.card: The disguised companion suddenly flies off as a bird; Nestor realizes a goddess has been guiding Telemachus and prays to her.

subs.text: Scene five.
Athena Reveals Herself at Pylos.
Night approaches and Nestor invites the guests to his palace.
Go with him, Telemachus, and sleep at the king's house.
But I will back to the ship, to hearten the crew, for I am the one old man among them;
and at dawn I go on to the Cauconians, where a debt is owed me, no new thing and no small one.
Dear boy, no fear that you prove base or weak, when gods walk beside you so young,
and that was no other of the Olympians but the daughter of Zeus himself,
the glorious grey-eyed one who honored your father among the Argives.
Be gracious, mistress:
grant fair fame to me, to my children, to my honored wife, and I will sacrifice to you a yearling heifer,
broad-browed, unbroken, her horns wrapped in gold.
At dawn a heifer is sacrificed.
Telemachus is bathed and dressed for departure.

sign.name: Limpid and opaque
sign.operation: Wide on the courtyard at dusk: Mentor's figure is replaced, on twos, by the eagle rising from the same mark; hold on the empty mark after.

scenes.world: The whitewashed royal courtyard from dusk to dawn, long shadows, then pale morning light, smoke from an altar; silent costume-drama texture.

captain.asks: Replace Mentor on the mark by the eagle rising, then hold the empty mark; dawn sacrifice and dressing follow.
diagnosis: The replacement does not happen on twos: there is a bird and an empty ground, never on the same mark.
The dawn ritual closes strongly: water poured, cloak fitted, real gestures.
The heifer is a carved relief in NOW; carvings keep standing in for living things.

scenes.title: The Chariot Road to Sparta
scenes.card: Nestor gives Telemachus horses and a chariot, and his son Pisistratus drives him overland toward Sparta.

subs.text: Scene six.
The Chariot Road to Sparta.
Quickly now, my sons, harness the flowing-maned horses to the car for Telemachus,
and let the housekeeper load bread and wine and such meats as kings' sons feed on.
He has far to drive before nightfall.
Pisistratus takes the reins beside him and drives out of Pylos.
Pisistratus spend the night at Phera under Diocles's hospitality.
At first light they yoked the horses again and drove out through gate and ringing portico,
all day through the wheatlands, until the sun sank and every road grew dark toward Lacedaemon.

sign.name: Liquid perception
sign.operation: Travelling shot beside the chariot, letting the landscape take the frame.

scenes.world: A dusty country road through rolling wheatfields and olive hills under high summer sun, long shadows at dawn and dusk; travelogue landscape.

captain.asks: Travel beside the chariot and let the landscape take the frame.
diagnosis: Landscape carries it: wheatfields, hills and a valley do the liquid perception the sign wants.
The chariot is a hay cart, a buggy, an engraving and a toy: never one vehicle.
Cars at a picnic and asphalt hairpins break the road to Sparta.

prologue: Telemachus lands at Pylos, kingdom of an old king who fought beside his father at Troy. He hopes to learn what happened to Odysseus after the war. Athena travels with him, still disguised as his father's old friend Mentor.

cast.name: Athena
cast.who: his protector goddess, disguised as Mentor

cast.who: old king of Pylos, fought at Troy

cast.name: Agamemnon
cast.who: leader of the war, murdered on returning

cast.name: Orestes
cast.who: Agamemnon's son, who avenged his father

carry: Nestor knew nothing certain, so Telemachus now heads to Sparta, to a king who came home last of all.
